__note: One line per table, hand-written, and the ONLY hand-written thing about a card.
The table NAMES and the schema blocks are parsed out of tools/schema_context.py at
load; a test asserts the key set here equals that parsed set, so this file cannot
drift the way the deleted ALLOWED_TABLES list did (19 names against 21 grants).
WRITTEN FOR AN EMBEDDING, NOT FOR A READER. These strings are what a shop owner's
question is scored against, so they use the words an owner would type -- 'past the
promised date', 'went out the door', 'work centres' -- rather than column names.
The British spelling in work_centers is deliberate: the eval asks 'which work
centre has the most operations queued' and an earlier arm answered by inventing

shipments and shipment_line_items name REVENUE and SALES on purpose. They are not in CORE_SPINE, so 'what is my revenue trend' has to reach them through this line alone -- and with the first draft of these purposes it did not: shipments ranked fifth, behind inventory_transactions and routing_operations, because no purpose said the word revenue anywhere.

purposes.companies: The tenant record for this shop: its own name and configuration flags.
purposes.customers: Who the shop sells to. Name is identity; archived customers have deleted_at set.
purposes.customer_addresses: Where a customer's invoices and deliveries are posted: their billing and delivery addresses.
purposes.vendors: Suppliers and outside-process providers the shop buys from. Identity only.
purposes.vendor_addresses: A vendor's postal addresses, one row per address.
purposes.parts: Parts and part numbers: every part the shop makes, buys or stocks, with its description, pricing and stock level.
purposes.part_pricing_tiers: Volume price breaks per part: what a part costs at each quantity band.
purposes.parts_bom: Bill of materials: which child parts and raw stock go into making a parent part.
purposes.parts_unit_conversions: How a part's purchase unit converts to its stocking or usage unit.
purposes.quotes: Prices offered to customers: status, expiry, and whether one turned into a job.
purposes.quote_line_items: The priced lines on a quote -- what was quoted, how many, at what price.
purposes.jobs: Work the shop has taken on: promised due date, production and fulfillment status, customer.
purposes.job_parts: The parts on a job -- quantity, unit price, line total, and all-in cost per unit.
purposes.shipments: Packing slips: what actually left the building, and when. Realised revenue and sales are dated from here — only shipped work counts.
purposes.shipment_line_items: How many of each job part actually shipped on a slip. Revenue is this quantity times the part's unit price.
purposes.job_operations: The steps of work inside a job: sequence, status, and which work centre runs each.
purposes.job_materials: The material a specific job part is expected to consume, snapshotted at job time.
purposes.work_centers: In-house machines, cells and benches -- work centres -- where operations are run.
purposes.vendor_services: A process an outside vendor performs, such as anodising, plating or heat treat.
purposes.routings: The manufacturing plan for a part: the ordered set of operations that make it.
purposes.routing_operations: One step in a part's standing routing: its sequence, the work centre that runs it, and standard times.
purposes.inventory_transactions: Stock movements against a part: material taken in, issued to jobs, and adjusted after a count.
purposes.material_lots: One mill heat of one raw material, created when the material is received. Answers traceability questions -- which heats a part has held, when they came in, and which vendor supplied them. Only parts with lot_tracked = true have lots at all, and most do not.
